name: Valid Email Verification for Contact Form 7
author: Sabirul Islam

sections.description:
Valid Email Verification for Contact Form 7 is a lightweight plugin that ensures users submit valid and unique email addresses in Contact Form 7 forms.

It helps prevent duplicate and fake email submissions, improving the quality of your form leads and reducing spam.

Important Notice: This plugin does not send verification emails or confirmation links. It validates submitted email addresses and prevents duplicate submissions according to the configured settings.

This plugin is independently developed and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Contact Form 7 team.

Features

  • Block duplicate email submissions in Contact Form 7
  • Validate email format and check against previously submitted emails before processing
  • New in 1.1.0: View and manage stored email submissions directly in the admin panel (Settings → Email Verification CF7 → Submissions tab)
  • New in 1.1.0: Customise the duplicate-email error message shown to users
  • New in 1.1.0: Per-form email field overrides for individual Contact Form 7 forms
  • New in 1.1.0: Automatic safe database migration — no re-activation required after updating
  • New in 1.1.0: Full GDPR compliance — integrates with WordPress Personal Data Exporter & Eraser
  • New in 1.1.0: WordPress Privacy Policy Guide integration (wp_add_privacy_policy_content)
  • Secure codebase (prepared statements, sanitization, escaping, nonce verification)
  • Lightweight, 100% local processing — no external API or third-party service required
  • Fully compatible with the latest WordPress and Contact Form 7 versions

Privacy Policy

  • Data Collected: Email address, Contact Form 7 form ID, and submission timestamp (created_at).
  • Purpose: Exclusively used to detect and prevent duplicate form submissions and curb form spam.
  • Storage Location: All data is stored locally in your WordPress database (wp_cf7_email_verifications table). No data is transmitted to external servers, third-party APIs, or remote services.
  • Retention Period: Records remain stored indefinitely to maintain duplicate prevention rules, until manually deleted by an administrator or erased upon user request.
  • Data Subject Rights (GDPR/CCPA): Fully compatible with WordPress Core’s Personal Data Exporter (Tools → Export Personal Data) and Personal Data Eraser (Tools → Erase Personal Data).
  • Privacy Policy Guide: Provides recommended privacy policy text under Settings → Privacy → Policy Guide.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/valid-email-verification-cf7/ directory, or install it directly via the WordPress plugin installer.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. The plugin works automatically with your Contact Form 7 forms — no extra configuration needed.
  4. To customise settings, go to Settings → Email Verification CF7.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Contact Form 7?

Yes. This plugin is specifically built for Contact Form 7 and requires it to be installed and active.

Does this plugin send verification emails or confirmation links?

No. This plugin does not send verification emails or confirmation links. It validates submitted email addresses and prevents duplicate submissions according to the configured settings.

How does the email verification work?

When a user submits a form, the plugin validates the email format, checks it against previously saved submissions in your local database, and prevents the submission if the email address was already used.

What email information is stored and why?

The plugin stores:
* The submitted email address.
* The Contact Form 7 form ID.
* The submission date and timestamp.

This data is stored solely to prevent duplicate and spam submissions across form entries. No passwords, IPs, names, or other personal fields are stored by this plugin.

How long is the email data retained?

Submitted email records are retained indefinitely in your WordPress database to enforce duplicate prevention rules, or until deleted by a site administrator or erased via a personal data erasure request.

How can administrators delete stored email data?

Administrators can delete stored data in three ways:
1. Single record deletion: Navigate to Settings → Email Verification CF7 → Submissions and click Delete next to any record.
2. WordPress GDPR Eraser: Go to Tools → Erase Personal Data, enter the user’s email address, and confirm erasure.
3. Plugin uninstallation: Deleting the plugin via the WordPress Plugins screen permanently removes the database table and all stored records.

Does this plugin support WordPress personal data exporter and eraser?

Yes. The plugin integrates natively with WordPress’s privacy tools under Tools → Export Personal Data and Tools → Erase Personal Data.

Will existing stored emails be lost when I update to 1.1.0?

No. Version 1.1.0 adds a new form_id column to the existing table using dbDelta, which is a non-destructive operation. All previously stored emails are preserved.

Can I customise the error message shown to users?

Yes. Since version 1.1.0 you can set a custom error message under Settings → Email Verification CF7.

Can I see which emails have been blocked?

Yes. The Submissions tab under Settings → Email Verification CF7 shows all stored email addresses, their submission date, and which form they came from. You can also delete individual records.

Will the plugin delete stored emails on uninstall?

Yes. If the user uninstalls the plugin (not just deactivates), the plugin removes its custom database table and all plugin options.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: Added prominent clarification — this plugin does not send verification emails or confirmation links; it validates and prevents duplicate email submissions.
  • New: Submissions tab in admin — view paginated list of all stored email submissions, see which form each came from, and delete individual records.
  • New: Customisable duplicate-email error message — override the default validation message directly from the settings page.
  • New: Per-form field override support — configure specific email field names for each Contact Form 7 form.
  • New: WordPress Privacy Tools integration — full support for WordPress Personal Data Exporter (Tools → Export Personal Data) and Personal Data Eraser (Tools → Erase Personal Data).
  • New: WordPress Privacy Policy Guide integration (wp_add_privacy_policy_content) with suggested policy text.
  • New: Automatic database migration — the plugin now tracks its DB schema version and runs dbDelta() safely on plugin update without requiring re-activation. Existing data is fully preserved.
  • New: form_id column added to the cf7_email_verifications table to record which CF7 form triggered each submission.
  • Improvement: Settings page now uses tabbed navigation (Settings / Submissions) with helpful guidance notice.
  • Improvement: Nonce verification added to all admin actions.
  • Improvement: Code refactored with improved inline documentation throughout.
  • Compatibility: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1 and Contact Form 7 6.x.

1.0.3

  • Update: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.2

  • Update: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.0.
  • Fix: Minor compatibility adjustments for the latest WP release.

1.0.1

  • Fix: Properly block duplicate email submissions before sending mail.
  • Fix: PHP 8.2 “dynamic property” notice resolved by declaring class properties.
  • Fix: Database query now uses $wpdb->get_var() with prepare() for SELECT COUNT(*).
  • Tweak: Improved sanitization, escaping, and code cleanup.

1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Added email verification for Contact Form 7.
  • Implemented security improvements.
